brief.title: The Salt Ledger
brief.premise: In a city built on a tidal flat, a debt-clerk discovers that the tide-bound magic that keeps the sea out is being quietly overdrawn, and must expose the guild hiding the shortfall before the next spring tide.
constraints: Magic must always carry a visible physical cost.

world.name: Saltmere
world.description: Saltmere is a walled city on a tidal flat where tide-bound magic holds back the sea and every working of it is recorded as a debt in the Salt Clerks' ledgers.

locations.name: Ledger Hall
locations.description: The counting-house where tide-debts are recorded in salt-ink ledgers, built on the highest ground of the flat.

locations.name: Drowned Quay
locations.description: A harbour district that floods twice daily, home to ferrymen and smugglers.

locations.name: Brine Gate
locations.description: The great sluice-wall holding back the sea, protected by tide-bound wardings renewed each month.

locations.name: Mudflat Market
locations.description: A market held on the flats.

factions.name: Salt Clerks
factions.description: A guild of accountants who record and ration tide-magic debts.

factions.name: Gate Wardens
factions.description: Warders who renew the wardings on the Brine Gate each month, paying for it with their own bodies.

rules.statement: Every working of tide-magic leaves a visible mark on the caster, such as salt-crusted skin or white hair.
Tide-bound wardings can be renewed only at the turn of a spring tide.
A tide-debt, once entered in the ledger, binds the debtor's family until it is paid.
Entries written in salt-ink cannot be altered without leaving a pale scar on the page.

history.name: The Founding of the Gate
history.description: Settlers raised the Brine Gate on the flat and bound it with the first tide-wardings.

history.name: The First Ledger
history.description: The Salt Clerks began recording tide-debts after the first warding renewal drained a ferryman's family of its savings.

history.name: The Great Flood
history.description: A warding lapsed and the sea flooded the Drowned Quay for a week, until the Gate Wardens renewed the wardings at the next spring tide.

history.name: The Market Charter
history.description: The Salt Clerks granted the Quay Ferrymen the right to trade on the flats at low tide in return for a levy.

conflicts.name: The Overdrawn Gate
conflicts.description: The Gate Wardens suspect the Salt Clerks of hiding how much tide-magic the Brine Gate has already consumed.

evidence_quotes: A market held on the flats.
labels.correction_hint: Optional: add detail; not a blocking defect.

evidence_summary: Three descriptions are bare but contradict nothing; thinness is not a defect.
